injuries.name: Beckett Sennecke
injuries.detail: Anaheim recalled Nico Myatovic from AHL San Diego in a corresponding move. Sennecke will miss at least the next three games, starting with Saturday's matchup against Utah, but it's unclear when he will be available to return. He has registered 12 goals, 26 points, 53 shots on net and 19 hits in 22 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Ryan Poehling
injuries.detail: Poehling is on long-term injured reserve, but he is eligible to be activated at any time. He's still expected to be out until early December, though he may beat that timeline by a small margin if his recovery continues to go well.

injuries.name: A.J. Greer
injuries.detail: Greer suffered an upper-body injury in Sunday's 6-3 win over Ottawa. He will miss at least the next four games, starting with Tuesday's matchup against Vancouver, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return. Greer has four goals, six points, 23 shots on net and 36 hits in 13 appearances this season.

injuries.name: James Hagens
injuries.detail: After being placed on injured reserve early Saturday morning, Hagens' timeline for recovery has been revealed to keep him sidelined for at least the next five or six games. It's an unfortunate break for the Bruins and the 20-year-old winger, as he had posted six goals, 12 points, 34 shots on net and 19 blocked shots over 17 games prior to going down. His absence might hurt his rookie of the year case in the long run, but once he's able to return, he'll give the Bruins' third line a major boost. In his absence, expect the newly recalled Michael Eyssimont, who was named the AHL's player of the month for October, to take his place.

injuries.name: Justin Danforth
injuries.detail: Danforth's move to IR allowed the Sabres to activate Sam Carrick (middle body) ahead of Thursday's game versus the Ducks. Danforth remains without a clear timeline to return to action. He will miss his fourth straight game Thursday and will be eligible to return whenever ready, as long as he doesn't later end up on long-term injured reserve.

injuries.name: Matt Grzelcyk
injuries.detail: Buffalo placed Grzelcyk on injured reserve Tuesday. He hasn't played since Opening Night against Columbus on Oct. 1. With Rasmus Dahlin (upper body) and Grzelcyk unavailable, the Sabres recalled Dennis Gilbert from AHL Rochester to play against Montreal on Tuesday.

injuries.name: Morgan Frost
injuries.detail: Frost was on the receiving end of a big hit from Ottawa's Tyler Kleven in the middle frame. Frost managed a couple of shifts after briefly going to the locker room following the hit, but he ultimately couldn't finish the game. Since there was no update on the 27-year-old's status, he can be considered day-to-day for now. Calgary will continue its five-game road trip in Pittsburgh on Wednesday.

injuries.name: Martin Pospisil
injuries.detail: After leaving Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to Chicago late in the second period with an upper-body injury, Pospisil won't play against Ottawa on Monday. It's unclear when he will be ready to return, but he could be out for a while. Pospisil has a concussion history, and the Flames may take a cautious approach with his recovery.

injuries.name: Connor Bedard
injuries.detail: Bedard and the Blackhawks elected to go the surgical route rather than rehabbing with respect to the 21-year-old's shoulder injury, and his recovery timeline has now come into focus. The 2023 No. 1 overall pick was placed on injured reserve Sunday, which freed up a roster spot for the team. Roman Kantserov has been centering the top line of late, and he looked good in that role with six points over the weekend in games against Calgary and Vancouver, so he could be the biggest beneficiary of Bedard's absence.

injuries.name: Wyatt Kaiser
injuries.detail: Kaiser won't be eligible to return until Chicago hosts Minnesota on Nov. 29. He has contributed two goals, five assists, 19 shots on net, 30 blocked shots and 20 hits in 23 appearances this season. With Kaiser unavailable, Kevin Korchinski will likely play against Vancouver on Sunday.

injuries.name: Bowen Byram
injuries.detail: Byram was previously ruled out for Saturday's matchup against Calgary, and he won't be available for Sunday's matchup against Vancouver. It's also doubtful that he will join the team for Wednesday's contest against Seattle. It remains unclear when he will be ready to return.

injuries.name: Nathan MacKinnon
injuries.detail: MacKinnon wouldn't be ready until mid-February if that timetable proves to be accurate. It can't be overstated how important MacKinnon is to the Avalanche. He finished each of the previous four regular seasons with over 110 points, and he was well on his way towards another elite campaign after scoring 10 goals and 30 points through 20 appearances. Brock Nelson and Nazem Kadri are serving as the Avalanche's top two centers while MacKinnon is unavailable.

injuries.name: Kyle Capobianco
injuries.detail: Dallas also recalled Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas on Saturday and placed Lian Bichsel (lower body) on injured reserve. Capobianco hasn't played since Oct. 27 against New Jersey. He hasn't earned a point in five appearances this season, but he has registered three shots on net, three blocked shots and two hits.

injuries.name: Lian Bichsel
injuries.detail: Dallas also recalled Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas on Saturday and moved Kyle Capobianco (leg) to long-term injured reserve. Bichsel is week-to-week after being injured in Thursday's 8-3 loss to Winnipeg. He has one assist, 10 shots on net, 24 blocked shots and 39 hits in 18 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Sam Montembeault
injuries.detail: Montembeault hasn't yet appeared in a regular-season game during the 2026-27 campaign, as he sustained a lower-body injury during practice in early October and has been on injured reserve since then. The Canadiens indicated in late October that the netminder had been upgraded to day-to-day, but it's not yet clear when he'll be able to make his season debut. After making a career-high 62 regular-season appearances for Montreal during the 2024-25 campaign, the 30-year-old went 10-8-4 with a 3.43 GAA and .872 save percentage across 25 regular-season outings with the Canadiens last year. The Red Wings already have John Gibson and Daniil Tarasov in the crease, but Gibson hasn't been particularly sharp early in the year, so Montembeault will likely have an opportunity to compete for playing time once he's healthy.

injuries.name: Simon Edvinsson
injuries.detail: Edvinsson is continuing to hold out for a new contract as a restricted free agent, with no clear end in sight. It's possible a trade materializes at some point, though he would still need to agree to terms on a new contract with a different NHL club. Last season, Edvinsson recorded nine goals and 16 assists in 72 regular-season contests.

injuries.name: Alec Regula
injuries.detail: Regula continues to work his way back from offseason surgery that caused him to miss the entire preseason. With the shift to LTIR, the 26-year-old defenseman can be expected to miss at least the next nine games, having already been out of action for one, though it could be longer, considering the team hasn't provided a specific update.

injuries.name: Frederik Andersen
injuries.detail: Andersen, who signed a one-year, $1 million contract with Edmonton in July, is still rehabbing from a knee injury. He posted a 16-14-5 record with a 3.05 GAA and an .874 save percentage in 35 appearances for Carolina during the 2025-26 regular season. Once he's ready to play in the 2026-27 campaign with the Oilers, Andersen could compete for starts with Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi.

injuries.name: Brad Marchand
injuries.detail: Marchand is slightly behind Aleksander Barkov (knee) in terms of his potential return date. Barkov should be back in the fold within the next three games, per head coach Paul Maurice on Saturday. The 38-year-old Marchand has appeared in only two games this season and hasn't been in the lineup since Oct. 6 against the Kings.

injuries.name: Aleksander Barkov
injuries.detail: Barkov has appeared in only two games this season and hasn't played since Oct. 1. However, he is close to returning to the lineup. Once activated by the Panthers from long-term injured reserve, Barkov should occupy a top-six role while seeing time on the power play and penalty kill.

injuries.name: Mike Matheson
injuries.detail: Matheson missed six straight games before returning to the lineup against Boston on Thursday. However, he was back on the shelf for Saturday's 4-1 loss to Colorado and will need more time to recover from his lingering injury. The 32-year-old defenseman has one goal, four assists, 16 shots on net, 16 blocked shots and five hits in nine appearances this season. With Matheson out, Adam Engstrom and David Reinbacher could compete for playing time.

injuries.name: Josh Anderson
injuries.detail: The Canadiens moved Anderson to the injured reserve list Sunday after he logged a season-low 10:46 of ice time in Saturday's 4-1 loss to Colorado. He has contributed eight goals, 12 points, 35 shots on net and 42 hits in 19 appearances this season. With Anderson and Chris Kreider (lower body) dealing with long-term injuries, Florian Xhekaj and Owen Beck could see regular minutes in Montreal's bottom-six forward group.

injuries.name: Anthony Mantha
injuries.detail: After being placed on long-term injured reserve on Wednesday, Mantha underwent surgery Monday to repair a throat fracture. Prior to sustaining the injury, the 32-year-old winger posted five goals, 10 points, 21 shots on net and 11 hits over 17 appearances this season. In his absence, Amadeus Lombardi and Lenni Hameenaho will likely continue to serve as depth options in New Jersey's forward room.

injuries.name: Seamus Casey
injuries.detail: Casey began the season on non-roster injured reserve due to knee surgery. This move to LTIR doesn't change his timeline -- he's already missed enough time to be eligible to return. He was slated to miss 6-8 weeks, so don't expect him to be ready until late November at the earliest.

injuries.name: Alberts Smits
injuries.detail: Smits landed on injured reserve in early November, which has caused him to miss the Rangers' last five games. The 18-year-old blueliner appeared in 17 contests prior to going down, where posted a minus-2 rating, eight shots on net, 16 hits and 10 blocked shots while averaging 14:29 of ice time. Given his current time line, he's expected to return sometime between late January and March. In his absence, Matthew Robertson and Scott Morrow should continue to see depth roles on the blue line.

injuries.name: Joe Veleno
injuries.detail: Although Veleno didn't participate in practice Friday, it was encouraging to see him on the ice ahead of the session. The 26-year-old has been on long-term injured reserve since early October, and he was initially expected to miss approximately three months, so it wouldn't be surprising to see the Rangers bring him along slowly as he continues his recovery process.

injuries.name: Hayden Hodgson
injuries.detail: Hodgson hasn't been skating and is expected to miss his fourth straight game against Calgary on Monday with a groin injury. has contributed one goal, three shots on net, 20 hits and 24 PIM in 10 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Andre Burakovsky
injuries.detail: Burakovsky has yet to join his teammates on the ice since getting hurt in late October, but this is a positive step in the right direction for the 31-year-old winger. In his eight appearances this year, Burakovsky has yet to register a point, recording four blocks, three hits and three shots while averaging just 11:00 of ice time, a career-low mark.

injuries.name: Warren Foegele
injuries.detail: Foegele has been sidelined since late October, and he initially carried a return timetable of 3-4 weeks. While he hasn't yet entered that window, the fact that he hasn't yet resumed skating suggests that he isn't particularly close to returning to game action. A better idea of the 30-year-old's timetable to return will likely come into focus once he's cleared to return to the ice.

injuries.name: William Eklund
injuries.detail: Eklund's timeline would seem to indicate that he will be out of action until the calendar flips to 2027, though it's possible he makes a late-December return if on the early side of his timeline. While the 24-year-old winger is already on injured reserve, he could be a candidate for long-term injured reserve if the Senators need the cap space to make a move.

injuries.name: Nikita Grebenkin
injuries.detail: Grebenkin's upper-body injury has been revealed to be an issue with his back, which he has successfully had repaired. The 23-year-old winger is expected to miss the majority of the 2026-27 campaign, but his current timeline for return, barring any setbacks, projects him back sometime after the All-Star break in mid-February. When he does return, Grebenkin will look to build off a positive rookie campaign, where he compiled four goals, 14 points, 32 shots on net, 86 hits and 17 blocked shots across 55 regular-season outings in 2025-26.

injuries.name: Bryan Rust
injuries.detail: Rust has been out of action for the Penguins' last 11 contests due to his lower-body injury. When healthy, the 34-year-old winger has played in seven contests in which he has notched three goals and two assists, including a pair of power-play points.

injuries.name: Elmer Soderblom
injuries.detail: Pittsburgh moved Soderblom to injured reserve Wednesday, and he has already missed the last two games. It's unclear when he will be ready to return to the lineup. Soderblom has contributed one assist, five shots on net, four blocked shots and 15 hits in six appearances this season.

injuries.name: Ryan Graves
injuries.detail: Graves will miss the beginning of the 2026-27 campaign, and it's unclear when he will be ready to return. He contributed one goal, 21 shots on net, 38 blocked shots and 23 hits in 22 regular-season appearances for Pittsburgh in 2025-26.

injuries.name: Igor Chernyshov
injuries.detail: Chernyshov remains on injured reserve and has missed the last 11 games after blocking a shot in Ottawa on Oct. 22. While an exact timeline for Chernyshov's return to the lineup hasn't been established, it's probably reasonable to assume that he will be out until sometime in December.

injuries.name: Quentin Musty
injuries.detail: Musty suffered an upper-body injury ahead of training camp and was expected to have a long-term absence. He's been on non-roster injured reserve to begin the regular season, and it's not yet clear when he'll be deemed healthy. Once the 21-year-old is cleared to return to game action, he'll presumably be sent to AHL San Jose.

injuries.name: Kyle Keyser
injuries.detail: The Sharks announced in mid-September that Keyser was facing a long-term absence due to an upper-body injury, so his placement on non-roster injured reserve isn't particularly surprising. Once he's cleared to return, the 27-year-old will likely report to AHL San Jose.

injuries.name: Jake O'Brien
injuries.detail: O'Brien has been on non-roster injured reserve since the start of the regular season, but he's been with the team in Seattle and has been skating off to the side recently. Despite the 19-year-old's recent on-ice activity, it doesn't appear as though he's particularly close to being cleared for game action.

injuries.name: Jared McCann
injuries.detail: McCann had one goal in five games before sitting out Saturday's 5-1 loss to Minnesota. He has earned five assists, eight points, 28 shots on net, three blocked shots and six hits in 11 appearances this season. With McCann unavailable, Kaapo Kakko moved up to the top line in Saturday's game.

injuries.name: Torey Krug
injuries.detail: Krug's move to long-term injured reserve was partially a financial decision, as it allows the Blues to exceed the salary cap by $4 million. The 35-year-old blueliner hasn't played since the 2023-24 campaign, but he hasn't officially ruled out a return. Regardless of when he decides to hang up his skates, the 13-year NHL veteran will be remembered as an excellent two-way player, as he currently sits at 483 points, 621 hits and 832 blocked shots across 778 regular-season outings.

injuries.name: Conor Geekie
injuries.detail: Geekie has missed the last two games after landing on injured reserve, and he is facing an extended absence. He has earned four goals, five points, 27 shots on net and 59 hits in 20 outings this season.

injuries.name: Colton Sissons
injuries.detail: Sissons still needs to be cleared for contact, but he will participate in Sunday's practice. He has missed the last six games, but he has been making progress in his recovery. Sissons has two goals, six points, 19 shots on net, 38 hits and 11 blocked shots in 19 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Kirill Marchenko
injuries.detail: Marchenko will wear a non-contact jersey during the morning skate, so a return to the lineup against the Blue Jackets on Saturday appears unlikely. He has missed the last 10 games, but seems to be progressing. Marchenko has earned six goals, 14 points, 35 shots on net and 20 hits in 14 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Cole McWard
injuries.detail: The Maple Leafs moved McWard onto the injured reserve list Friday. He hasn't picked up a point in two NHL outings this season, but he has earned one shot on net, three blocked shots and one hit.

injuries.name: Nick Blankenburg
injuries.detail: Blankenburg is expected to participate in Saturday's morning skate, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return to the lineup. He is currently on injured reserve and hasn't played since Oct. 22. Blankenburg has one goal, six shots on net, six hits and two blocked shots in six appearances this campaign.

injuries.name: Miles Wood
injuries.detail: This move was necessary to create cap space for the activation of Dakota Joshua (abdomen) from LTIR. Wood has had no established timeline for a return, but he will be required to miss at least three more games.

injuries.name: John Marino
injuries.detail: Marino remains day-to-day and has been skating, but he isn't quite ready to return to the lineup. He will miss his 16th straight game against Winnipeg on Monday. Once he receives clearance to play, Marino will need to be activated from injured reserve.

injuries.name: Nate Schmidt
injuries.detail: The Mammoth indicated Monday that Schmidt was considered out indefinitely, and he was officially placed on injured reserve. It isn't particularly surprising to see him labeled as week-to-week, and it indicates that he's unlikely to return after spending the minimum amount of time on IR. It seems likely that the 35-year-old will be sidelined until at least late November.

injuries.name: Brendan Gallagher
injuries.detail: Gallagher will miss at least the next three games, starting with Saturday's matchup against Minnesota, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return. He has collected three assists, 26 shots on net, eight blocked shots and 32 hits in 21 appearances this campaign.

injuries.name: Dylan DeMelo
injuries.detail: DeMelo has already been placed on injured reserve, but this latest update provides a clearer recovery timeline. The blueliner hasn't scored a goal since Opening Night versus Boston, a stretch of 19 games without finding the back of the net. During that stretch, DeMelo did chip in seven helpers, 27 hits and 22 blocks, giving him decent category coverage in banger formats.
